feature: Local destination threat-list check of real outbound connections on macOS
authorization: The owner requested this one-time check in chat and chose a fresh public-list download one hour after the previous provider request; disclosure was limited to anonymous counts
configuration: Temporary settings outside the repository: outbound_connections.enabled, ip_threats.enabled and allow_updates, history disabled, default cache directory. The owner's own settings file was neither read nor changed.

list_update.requests: One GET per fixed IPv4/IPv6 URL; no observed identifiers were sent
list_update.cache: Default per-user state folder, created by this update below an existing parent

warnings: Socket observations only: direction, actual transmissions and safety are unverified; short-lived connections may be missed
Public threat-list matches are warnings, not proof of infection or transmission. No match does not prove safety.

interpretation: None of the 36 observed public destinations was in the fresh lists. This is a warning check, not a safety verdict.

privacy.connections: Observed only for this check; the CLI JSON was piped into an anonymous summariser and never written to disk

limitations: One 10-second observation on one Mac; short-lived connections may be missed
The lists cover hijacked or criminal-operated network blocks only, not individual malicious hosts or command-and-control servers
No listed destination was observed, so a real match, its process attribution and the matched warning path remain verified with synthetic data only
Local CLI only: the anonymous MCP tool, saved history details and the dashboard were not run against real connections
Linux and Windows real-host acceptance and browser checks remain separate
repository_data: Anonymous counts, public list metadata and hashes, fixed states and code hashes only; no IPs, ports, process names, PIDs, paths or host names

ci_run_after_push.tests: macOS, Ubuntu and Windows on Python 3.11, 3.14 and 3.15 each ran 611 tests without failures (skipped: 7 macOS, 8 Ubuntu, 77 Windows); all npm launcher jobs succeeded
ci_run_after_push.scope: Documentation-only commit; CI confirms the tree, not the real-connection check, which CI does not run

follow_up_anonymous_mcp.scope: Actual local SDK stdio on two Python versions: anonymity/non-persistence verified; both observations partial due to invalid_rows; no live updater or detail-history/browser test
